segments.name: Consumer Packaging
segments.description: Makes rigid paper, metal and plastic packaging for consumer staples customers in food, beverage, household, personal and pharmaceutical markets.
segments.evidence: Products within the Consumer Packaging segment consist of rigid packaging (paper, metal, and plastic), primarily serving the consumer staples market focused on food, beverage, household, personal, and pharmaceutical products.

segments.name: Industrial Paper Packaging
segments.description: Produces recycled-fiber packaging such as tubes, cores and paperboard, serving consumer staples, consumer discretionary and industrial end markets.
segments.evidence: Products within the Industrial Paper Packaging segment consist primarily of goods produced from recycled fiber including paperboard tubes, cores, cones and cans; partitions; paper-based protective materials; and uncoated recycled paperboard for high-end applications such as folding cartons, can board, and laminated structures.

segments.name: All Other
segments.description: Holds the remaining industrial and specialty plastics business after the ThermoSafe divestiture.
segments.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the operations in All Other consisted of approximately 5 plants in the Company's industrial and specialty plastics business.

revenueModel.text: Sonoco sells engineered packaging products directly to consumer and industrial customers, and also sells surplus manufactured paper to third parties.
revenueModel.evidence: Sonoco uses approximately 56% of the paper it manufactures, and the remainder is sold to third parties.

changes.text: In 2025 Sonoco sold TFP, which is presented as discontinued operations for all periods.
changes.evidence: On April 1, 2025, the Company completed the sale of TFP to TOPPAN Holdings Inc. ("Toppan") for approximately $1.8 billion on a cash-free and debt-free basis and subject to customary adjustments.

changes.text: In 2025 Sonoco sold ThermoSafe, leaving industrial and specialty plastics as the only All Other business, which moves into Industrial Paper Packaging in 2026.
changes.evidence: On November 3, 2025, the Company completed the sale of ThermoSafe, its temperature-assured packaging business and part of the All Other group of businesses, to Arsenal Capital Partners ("Arsenal"), a private equity firm, for net cash consideration of $656 million paid at closing on a cash-free and debt-free basis and subject to customary adjustments.
